Portrait Mode engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Portrait Mode rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app depth-of-field capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Portrait Mode — Apple Camera feature that captures still photos with shallow depth of field — soft background blur with the subject in sharp focus on supported iPhone models. Labeled 人像模式 or 人像 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • Depth of Field & background blur — computational depth maps and segmentation that isolate the subject from the background. Your listing may mention Depth of Field or Bokeh; building blur pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Studio Light portrait lighting (within Portrait Mode) — Natural Light, Studio Light, Stage Light, and Studio Light Mono effects applied to still portraits inside Portrait Mode. zh-Hans system UI often uses 影棚灯光, 自然光, or 舞台光. These are portrait lighting styles inside Portrait Mode — not a separate Studio Light product page.
  • AVFoundation & depth capture — camera session code that reads depth data and drives the portrait viewfinder. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Portrait Mode value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Portrait Mode support in the binary.

A working Portrait Mode story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Portrait Mode vs Photographic Styles vs Cinematic Mode vs Night Mode vs Macro vs Action Mode vs Center Stage vs Continuity Camera — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge eight Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Portrait Mode — shallow depth-of-field still photography with optional Studio Light portrait lighting inside Portrait Mode — not tone presets, not cinematic video blur, not low-light modes, not macro close-ups, not video stabilization, not auto framing, and not webcam portrait routing:

  • Portrait Mode & depth-of-field stills (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Portrait Mode", "Portrait", "Depth of Field", "Background blur", "Bokeh", "Subject focus", "Studio Light", "Natural Light", "Stage Light", 人像模式, 人像, 景深, 背景虚化, 影棚灯光. Still-photo shallow depth of field — soft background blur with subject in focus.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, Rich Contrast, Vibrant, Warm, Cool, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度, 鲜明, 暖色, 冷色. Photo color grading — not portrait background blur. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not still-photo Portrait Mode.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light photography — not daytime portrait blur marketing.
  • Macro listing copy (different) — extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance: Macro, Macro Control, 微距, 微距近拍. Close-up detail shots — not portrait background blur. Covered on our Macro guide.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖. Video stabilization — not still-photo portrait blur. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Center Stage listing copy (different) — auto framing that keeps you centered during FaceTime and video calls: Center Stage, 人物居中, 居中构图. Pan-and-track video framing — not still-photo depth-of-field blur. Covered on our Center Stage guide.
  • Continuity Camera portrait framing (different) — iPhone-as-Mac-webcam with optional portrait background blur during Mac video calls. Webcam routing story — not iPhone Camera still-photo Portrait Mode marketing. Covered on our Continuity Camera guide.

Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on still photos. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Action Mode stabilizes handheld video. Center Stage auto-frames video calls. Continuity Camera routes iPhone camera to Mac. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Portrait Mode-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Depth-of-field listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Portrait Mode features — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Portrait Mode phrasing

US pages use "Portrait Mode", "Portrait", "Depth of Field", "Background blur", "Bokeh", or "Subject focus." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 人像模式 for the feature, 人像 for people-focused portraits, and 景深 or 背景虚化 for depth-of-field blur. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing portrait capabilities your app does not support.

Studio Light inside Portrait Mode

When your English listing markets Studio Light, Natural Light, Stage Light, or Studio Light Mono as portrait lighting effects inside Portrait Mode, zh-Hans overlays may use 影棚灯光, 自然光, 舞台光, or 单色舞台光 — lighting styles within Portrait Mode, not a separate Studio Light product story. Do not split Studio Light into its own listing page when your screenshots show it inside the Portrait lighting picker.

Before-and-after blur comparisons

Portrait marketing often shows side-by-side standard vs Portrait Mode frames. Chinese buyers expect concise labels: 人像模式对比, 背景虚化效果, or 景深虚化 — not English "Before / After" pasted through machine translation without context.

Subject types per frame

Screenshot overlays differ by subject — people portraits, pet portraits, product shots with blur. Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 人像虚化 for people, 宠物人像 for pets, 产品景深 for product isolation — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Do not conflate with Photographic Styles, Cinematic Mode, or Macro

Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on still photos. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Macro captures extreme close-ups at minimum focus distance. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need portrait search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 人像模式, 人像, and 景深 each signal different intent from Photographic Styles 摄影风格 keywords or Macro 微距 keywords.

  • Subtitle — one clause on portrait or blur outcome; room for 人像模式 or 景深 within 30 characters — e.g. "人像模式，背景虚化" or "景深虚化，主体清晰"
  • Keywords — mix 人像模式, 人像, 景深, 背景虚化, and category nouns (摄影, 相机); avoid English-only "Portrait" stuffing — see Simplified Chinese keywords
  • Description — lead with the portrait blur workflow; mention Studio Light only when your app actually supports that Portrait lighting effect or equivalent depth-of-field capture

No. Depth-of-field capture, background blur, and Studio Light portrait lighting inside Portrait Mode control device behavior — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback.

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English Portrait Mode marketing originals.

Can AppLocale implement Portrait Mode or depth-map segmentation?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Portrait blur engineering, Studio Light rendering, and blur-comparison photo design are outside AppLocale scope.

How is this different from Photographic Styles, Cinematic Mode, Night Mode, Macro, Action Mode, Center Stage, or Continuity Camera?

Portrait Mode copy markets shallow depth-of-field still photography — 人像模式, 人像, 景深, 影棚灯光. Photographic Styles copy markets still-photo tone presets — 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Cinematic Mode copy markets shallow-depth cinematic video — 浅景深电影效果视频. Night Mode copy markets low-light capture — 夜间模式. Macro copy markets extreme close-ups — 微距, 微距近拍. Action Mode copy markets handheld video stabilization — 动作模式, 运动防抖. Center Stage copy markets auto framing on video calls — 人物居中. Continuity Camera copy markets iPhone-as-Mac-webcam portrait framing. Each surface has separate screenshot vocabulary.
